A session's live stream and its history in pages.

## Stream a session

`GET /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/stream` (SDK method `streamSession`)

The session as `@harbour/protocol` frames: `hello`, then a `snapshot` of its state and latest items (or, with `after`, the deltas after that cursor when the stream still holds them), then a `delta` for every change, live. Fold them with the protocol's `applyFrames`. Over a WebSocket, compressed where the platform can, or as server-sent events.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sessionId` | string | yes | The session's ID. |

**Query parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `after` | string | no | Resume after this cursor (a snapshot's or a delta's): the stream sends the deltas after it, or a snapshot when it no longer holds them. |

**Answers**

- `101`: [ServerFrame](/api/reference/types/#serverframe)[] (`application/json`). Upgraded to a WebSocket (send `Upgrade: websocket`). Each message is a JSON array of frames; an empty array is a keep-alive. The server negotiates `permessage-deflate` where the platform can. The client sends nothing; to resume, reconnect with `?after=` and the last cursor it holds.
- `200`: [ServerFrame](/api/reference/types/#serverframe) (`text/event-stream`). The stream. Without an upgrade: server-sent events, each named after its frame's type with the frame as its JSON data, then one `ready` event once the client has caught up. Snapshot and delta events carry their cursor as the event ID, so `Last-Event-ID` resumes too.

**Errors**: `400` invalid, `401` unauthenticated, `403` forbidden, `404` not_found. Each is an [ErrorBody](/api/reference/types/#errorbody).

## Page back through a session

`GET /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/history` (SDK method `getSessionHistory`)

The session's transcript in pages, newest first, for scrolling back past a snapshot's items: start with `before` set to the snapshot's `items[0].id`, then follow `nextCursor`.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sessionId` | string | yes | The session's ID. |

**Query parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cursor` | string | no | A previous page's `nextCursor`. |
| `before` | string | no | Items older than this item ID, such as a snapshot's `items[0].id`. |
| `limit` | integer | no | At most this many items. Default 50, cut to 200. (minimum 1) |

**Answers**

- `200`: [SessionHistoryPage](/api/reference/types/#sessionhistorypage) (`application/json`). One page of items.

**Errors**: `400` invalid, `401` unauthenticated, `403` forbidden, `404` not_found, `501` not_supported. Each is an [ErrorBody](/api/reference/types/#errorbody).

## Read an image in a session's transcript

`GET /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/images/{imageId}` (SDK method `getSessionImage`)

The bytes of an image a tool item names by reference (`images[].url`), such as a screenshot or a generated image: snapshots, deltas and history pages carry the reference, not the image. `imageId` is the SHA-256 of the image's bytes in lowercase hex, so the same URL always answers the same bytes, and the answer may be cached for good (`cache-control: private, max-age=31536000, immutable`). The model still reads the image itself. Needs viewer on the session; an ID the session's transcript doesn't name is `not_found`.

**Path parameters**

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sessionId` | string | yes | The session's ID. |
| `imageId` | string | yes | The SHA-256 of the image's bytes, in lowercase hex. |

**Answers**

- `200`: bytes, as `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/webp`, `image/gif`. The image, as its own type.

**Errors**: `400` invalid, `401` unauthenticated, `403` forbidden, `404` not_found. Each is an [ErrorBody](/api/reference/types/#errorbody).
